title: Ashiaa Store
context: A clean, minimalist online bookstore and stationery platform built for real active users
problem: Traditional online bookstores often suffer from cluttered interfaces, inconsistent typography, and poor component reusability, leading to low user retention and sluggish navigation.
approach: Architected a minimalist front-end using Atomic Design methodology with a strict design system, reusable component architecture, and Arabic-first typography tailored for custom stationery and books.

decisions.title: Ashiaa Store (متجر أشياء)
decisions.context: As Texon's flagship production project, this e-commerce platform required a robust design system and component architecture capable of handling active users while serving as a scalable foundation for future Texon web applications.

decisions.title: Atomic Design Methodology
decisions.why: Organized the codebase into atoms, molecules, and organisms to guarantee high reusability and maintain strict design system compliance across all pages.
decisions.alternatives: Standard flat component folder structure without strict modular hierarchy.

decisions.title: Custom Arabic Typography System
decisions.why: Paired 'Aref Ruqaa' for elegant headers with 'Tajawal' for clean UI body text to deliver an authentic, highly readable Arabic e-commerce aesthetic.
decisions.alternatives: Generic system fonts or single-font implementation.

decisions.title: Proprietary Color System Variables
decisions.why: Established dedicated accent hues (#CEB597, #724742) to enforce visual consistency and streamline theme maintenance across all interactive components.
decisions.alternatives: Hardcoded utility colors or unstructured CSS values.

tradeoffs.gained: Unmatched component reusability and seamless design consistency across the entire storefront.
tradeoffs.sacrificed: Higher initial setup time spent establishing the design system tokens and atomic architecture before writing feature code.

tradeoffs.gained: Enhanced user engagement and brand recognition through customized Arabic-first typography.
tradeoffs.sacrificed: Additional custom web font rendering overhead requiring optimization for initial page loads.

challenges.title: Design System Enforcement
challenges.description: Maintaining strict adherence to custom color scales, spacing, and atomic hierarchies across diverse product categories (books, office supplies, stationery) without code duplication.

challenges.title: RTL & Arabic UI Layouts
challenges.description: Ensuring responsive, accessible, and visual harmony in Right-to-Left (RTL) navigation while maintaining clean visual symmetry across varied screen sizes.

improvements: Migrate to Next.js App Router for Server-Side Rendering (SSR) to boost SEO and product indexing.
Integrate automated UI component testing using Storybook and Jest.
Implement dynamic search auto-suggestions and advanced multi-category filters.

title: StoreIt - Storage Management Platform
context: Modern cloud file management & sharing platform with dynamic storage analytics
problem: Users struggle with fragmented file management systems that lack intuitive search, unified media previewing, and real-time storage usage breakdowns.
approach: Built a full-stack file storage management application leveraging Next.js 15 App Router and Appwrite BaaS, featuring secure multi-format file uploads, dynamic global search, and instant file sharing.

decisions.title: StoreIt - Storage Management
decisions.context: This platform required handling multi-format file uploads, secure access permissions, and dynamic storage aggregation while delivering a lightning-fast responsive interface using the latest React 19 and Next.js 15 features.

decisions.title: Appwrite BaaS for Backend & Storage
decisions.why: Utilized Appwrite for streamlined user authentication, bucket storage management, and database queries without managing complex server infrastructure.
decisions.alternatives: Custom Node.js/Express backend with AWS S3 integration or Firebase.

decisions.title: Next.js 15 App Router Architecture
decisions.why: Leveraged Server Components and Server Actions for optimal data fetching, improved security around API keys, and faster initial page loads.
decisions.alternatives: Pages Router or client-side single-page application (SPA).

decisions.title: ShadCN UI & Tailwind CSS Design System
decisions.why: Allowed rapid construction of accessible, highly customized dashboard components and data visualization layouts with minimal CSS bundle size.
decisions.alternatives: Heavy monolithic UI frameworks like Material UI or Ant Design.

tradeoffs.gained: Rapid full-stack development velocity and built-in security for authentication and bucket permissions via Appwrite.
tradeoffs.sacrificed: Less flexibility for custom deep database queries compared to a raw PostgreSQL/Prisma ORM backend.

tradeoffs.gained: Bleeding-edge performance and developer experience using React 19 and Next.js 15 capabilities.
tradeoffs.sacrificed: Potential edge-case framework bugs due to using newly released major versions.

challenges.title: Dynamic Storage Breakdown Aggregation
challenges.description: Calculating and categorizing consumed vs. remaining storage in real time across multiple file formats (documents, images, videos, audio) without impacting dashboard load times.

challenges.title: Global Search & Client-Side Filtering
challenges.description: Implementing seamless cross-platform file searching and instant sorting (by date, name, or size) across dynamic dataset queries.

improvements: Add drag-and-drop file upload queues with progress indicators for large files.
Implement granular file permission controls (read-only vs. edit access for shared links).
Integrate automated image compression before Appwrite bucket storage upload.

title: Texon Official Portfolio
context: A minimalist, high-performance agency showcase built with modular React architecture
problem: Agency portfolios often suffer from bloated codebases, slow page loads, and tangled section logic, leading to difficult maintenance and poor visual performance.
approach: Engineered a lightning-fast, ultra-clean web experience using React + Vite and Tailwind CSS, enforced with a strict modular folder architecture separating UI tokens, layout components, and section logic.

decisions.title: Texon Agency Platform
decisions.context: As the primary digital storefront for Texon software agency, this project needed to showcase elite engineering standards, sub-second load times, and a future-proof architecture for expanding client case studies.

decisions.title: Vite + React Bundling Architecture
decisions.why: Chosen over heavy full-stack frameworks to achieve instant HMR during development and minimal production bundle footprint for sub-second page loads.
decisions.alternatives: Standard Create React App or Next.js static site generation.

decisions.title: Strict Modular Folder Architecture
decisions.why: Organized the codebase into distinct layers (`components/layout`, `components/ui`, `sections/`, `helpers/`) to keep pure utility functions isolated from UI rendering and maximize code maintainability.
decisions.alternatives: Flat component structure or feature-based grouping without layer boundaries.

decisions.title: Custom Logic Helpers & SEO Wrappers
decisions.why: Abstracted analytics, meta tags, and data fetching into dedicated helper modules (`/helpers`) to enforce consistent SEO defaults and DRY clean code standards across all pages.
decisions.alternatives: Inline meta tags and repeated fetching logic directly inside page components.

tradeoffs.gained: Blazing fast initial load speed, zero runtime overhead, and a clean codebase that scales seamlessly for new team members.
tradeoffs.sacrificed: No built-in Server-Side Rendering (SSR) out of the box compared to Next.js.

tradeoffs.gained: Strict separation of concerns where UI updates never leak into helper or utility logic.
tradeoffs.sacrificed: Slightly higher overhead when organizing initial project folder structures and routing setups.

challenges.title: Scalable Section & UI Component Isolation
challenges.description: Structuring complex section layouts into self-contained subcomponent folders without creating circular dependencies or component duplication.

challenges.title: Global State & SEO Configuration
challenges.description: Managing centralized route constants, global color variables, and dynamic metadata across dynamic client showcase routes cleanly.

improvements: Implement dynamic page transitions and interactive micro-animations using Framer Motion.
Add interactive case study previews with dynamic filtering by service category.
Integrate automated lighthouse performance auditing into the CI/CD deployment pipeline.
